misreadings.quote: He is indignant that his years of devotion are discarded after a single missed train
misreadings.evidence: "Why did Gregor have to be the only one condemned to work for a company where they immediately became highly suspicious at the slightest shortcoming?"
misreadings.explanation: Gregor complains about the company's suspicion and the chief clerk's visit, but nothing in the text says his years of service have been discarded or that anyone has dismissed him.

misreadings.quote: Gregor hopes the thump was soft, muffled by the carpet
misreadings.evidence: "There was a loud thump, but it wasn't really a loud noise. His fall was softened a little by the carpet, and Gregor's back was also more elastic than he had thought, which made the sound muffled and not too noticeable."
misreadings.explanation: The narrator reports the softened, muffled sound as a fact; Gregor is not described as hoping for it after the fall, since his earlier worry was about the noise he was bound to make.

misreadings.quote: he hasn't come to offer help but to witness and document a failure of productivity
misreadings.evidence: "did the chief clerk have to come himself, and did they have to show the whole, innocent family that this was so suspicious that only the chief clerk could be trusted to have the wisdom to investigate it?"
misreadings.explanation: The chief clerk's purpose is only Gregor's resentful guess that he has come to investigate; the text never says he has come to document a failure and not to help.

result.note: The reflection is largely faithful, with interpretive or metaphorical framing that is acceptable, and only a few low-severity overstatements or misattributions.
